rules.rule: Check for occupational sharps/splash exposure to body fluids
rules.problem: Type and structure are right: trigger (sharps injury OR splash) and check_for covers every fluid in the red box. Two scope qualifiers from the heading are not encoded: 'health worker' (no finding form exists; the rule fires for any patient with a sharps injury or fluid exposure) and the splash route 'eye/mouth/nose/broken skin' (c002). Both widen the trigger slightly; the clinical response (PEP assessment) is the same, so this is acceptable if recorded.

rules.rule: Urgent: occupational sharps/splash exposure to body fluids
rules.problem: Urgent is justified by 'Give urgent attention'. The (and (or sharps, splash) (or fluids...)) structure matches the heading 'with a sharps injury or splash ... with exposure to any of'. Same two dropped qualifiers as the task ('health worker', splash route), so the Urgent priority also applies to a non-health-worker or to a splash onto intact skin.

rules.rule: Diagnose possible TB from TB symptoms (occupational infection control)
rules.problem: 'possible' matches 'patients with possible TB'; the or-structure matches the footnote's 'cough, fever ≥ 2 weeks, unexplained weight loss or drenching night sweats'; the 2-week window is applied to fever with the correct comparison direction. Only the dropped 'drenching' qualifier (c032) and the ambiguity of whether the 2-week window also covers cough (c029) remain.

summary: No invented or wrong content: every condition traces to the red box or the TB-symptom footnote and all 20 SNOMED concepts exist. The main weakness is the splash trigger (c002/c016): 'Exposure to blood and/or body fluid' loses the eye/mouth/nose/broken-skin route, and the 'health worker' scope of the heading is not encoded, so the task and the Urgent evaluation fire slightly more broadly than the page. Three substances are nearest-available approximations (Serosanguinous fluid for blood-stained fluid/tissue, Exudate for wound secretions) and 'drenching' is dropped from night sweats; no closer SNOMED concepts exist for any of them.
